summary: a wave's merge carries up to mergeBatch finished spans of its own tick, cherry-picked in order and gated once; red or a conflict resets to the tip and merges them one at a time
acceptance: a green batch ships every span in one ledger commit after one afterMerge gate run; a red batch, or a conflict while picking, resets to the tip before the batch and merges its spans individually, so blame and revert stay per entry
tests: a merge carries up to mergeBatch finished spans of the same tick
a sibling tick's spans are never carried in this tick's batch
a green batch ships every span in one ledger commit
a batch whose afterMerge gates red resets to the tip and merges its spans one at a time
a conflict while picking a batch falls back to per-entry merging
the afterMerge gates run once over a green batch
notes: Only spans waiting on the ship lock are candidates. A red batch costs one gate run more than merging serially would have — that is the priced trade, not a defect to design around.
